entries.title: Watch the winning trailer from the Future Vision XPRIZE, The Gifted.
entries.summary: Watch the winning trailer from the Future Vision XPRIZE, The Gifted.
entries.content:
Earlier this year, we partnered with XPRIZE and Range Media Partners to launch the Future Vision XPRIZE, a global competition calling for films that envision a hopeful, technology-enabled future. Last week in Los Angeles, independent filmmaker Jeff Synthesized was named the grand prize winner for The Gifted.

Inspired by a deeply personal story, the film centers on an 11-year-old boy who recreates his late mother’s voice and essence out of love and code. What emerges across the town’s networks quietly cares for his entire community — reflecting the filmmaker’s belief that technology’s greatest promise lies in empathy and human connection.

Chosen from more than 2,500 entries worldwide, the solo-developed project receives $100,000 alongside $2.5 million in feature production funding. Through Google’s 100 ZEROS initiative, we are partnering with Range Media Partners to help bring this story to the big screen.

entries.title: Google Arts & Culture turns 15 — and gives its app a makeover
entries.summary: Celebrating 15 years of Google Arts & Culture with a new app experience YouTube video
entries.content:
Over the past 15 years, Google Arts & Culture has partnered with more than 3,000 cultural institutions and artists across more than 90 countries. Working alongside this vibrant ecosystem, our goal has always been to preserve and make the world’s art and culture accessible to everyone, while creating experiences that educate, inspire, and delight.

Starting today, you can check out our refreshed Google Arts & Culture mobile app to mark this 15-year milestone. The updated experience helps you easily navigate our partners’ vast archives, including high-resolution artworks, archaeological 3D artifacts, fashion, performance art, sports, craft, culinary heritage, natural history, science, design, and nature.

A new way to ask and see

At the heart of this update is a new conversational search: ask any question about arts and culture, and get an answer that pairs insightful explanations with visuals and curated stories from partner archives.

Ask anything that sparks your curiosity — whether you're delving into ‘Caravaggio’s chiaroscuro,’ finding ‘impressionist museums in Paris,’ browsing ‘images captured by the Webb telescope,’ wondering ‘what are bento boxes,’ or simply taking a moment to admire ‘cats in art.’

Ask questions in your own words, and get visual, grounded answers.

An all-new homepage

The redesigned homepage brings together the entire app into a single feed built for quick daily discovery. Modular sections surface bite-sized cultural stories, daily highlights, and direct access to interactive features. This includes two new AI experiments: Chrono Look, which lets you virtually try on historical attire across different eras through sketches and realistic renderings, and Dial-an-Artist, an interactive tool for simulated conversations with historical figures about their work. Plus, check out an expanded City Guide, featuring 27 newly added destinations with local cultural landmarks and real-time cultural events.

The updated Google Arts & Culture app is rolling out globally starting today. Download or update now on Google Play and the Apple App Store to explore the next chapter of cultural discovery.

entries.title: See what 4 builders are making with Gemini 3.8 Flash
entries.summary: A collage of four digital 3D visualization projects showing two views of globe satellite maps, a dinosaur skeleton model, and an exploded view of a mechanical transmission diagram with labeled components.
entries.content:
Gemini 3.8 Flash is our most intelligent workhorse model, delivering significant improvements from 3.7 Flash across software engineering, agentic tasks, and critical, multistep reasoning in specialized domains. These performance gains stem from a core design choice: 3.8 Flash works harder. On complex tasks, it exhibits greater diligence — executing extra reasoning steps and calling tools iteratively to land a more accurate output.

Builders have been creating with Gemini 3.8 Flash since we launched it and new audio models this month. From developing simulations to testing visual reasoning, check out some of the coolest builds and experiments from the community so far.

Create a model rocket simulation.

Ashutosh Shrivastava (@ai_for_success on X) used Gemini 3.8 Flash and Google Antigravity to map the live paths of satellites, space stations, and orbital rockets.

Animate an ink painting.

Noctus (@noctus91 on X) used Gemini 3.8 Flash’s multimodal capabilities to transform Seigaiha waves — a traditional Japanese pattern — into what looks like a moving ink painting.

Create a 3D dinosaur skeleton.

Gemini 3.8 Flash delivers substantial gains on multistep reasoning in STEM and other fields. Emily (@IamEmily2050 on X) pushed these capabilities, asking the model to create a T. rex skeleton with a four-phase prompt, complete with strict requirements, banned shortcuts, and accuracy checks.

Build an automatic transmission simulation from scratch.

Hakm (@hakmgpt on X) gave Gemini 3.8 Flash an engineering challenge: Build an interactive model of an automatic transmission. His prototype involves 10 camera views, four display modes, smart labels, and a side panel that teaches you more about any transmission part you click on.

Gemini 3.8 Flash delivers substantial gains from 3.7 Flash, often approaching the performance of higher-cost frontier models. Try it across Google products and tools, including Google Antigravity and Google AI Studio.

entries.title: 3 ways this grocer cooks for 200 guests with Gemini
entries.summary: How Edy’s Grocer Caters for 200 Guests YouTube video
entries.content:
Running Edy’s Grocer in Greenpoint, Brooklyn, means balancing a buzzing deli counter with catering, pop-ups, and community events. As owner Edy Massih has learned, scaling his family’s delicious Lebanese recipes into giant party spreads quickly creates operational bottlenecks.

To skip kitchen math and streamline workflow, Edy uses Gemini as an on-demand sous-chef and strategist. Here are three ways Gemini keeps Edy’s kitchen running efficiently:

1. Scale recipes without kitchen math errors.

Hand-calculating measurements wastes time and risks costly errors with delicate spices and pastry ratios. “You can't just multiply ingredients by 50,” says Edy. “You'll ruin the dish.” Instead of scribbling math on scrap paper, Edy uses Gemini to convert family recipes into bulk catering batches instantly. Gemini scales every ingredient, so the team can start prep immediately.

Try this to scale your recipes: Scale a recipe for chicken shawarma wraps from 8 servings up to 50 for a large event, adjusting spices so they don't overpower the dish, and group ingredients by grocery aisle.

2. Auto-generate shopping lists.

Building catering grocery runs usually requires manually combining ingredients across recipes. Edy turns to Gemini to convert event menus into organized, aisle-by-aisle prep sheets, total shared ingredients, and structure prep schedules days in advance. “It serves up precise ingredient breakdowns and creates a complete shopping list with everything I'd need, all while keeping our food waste and cost to a minimum,” says Edy.

Try this to autogenerate your shopping lists: Create a grocery shopping list for a large mezze platter serving 10 to 12 people. Include dips like hummus, baba ganoush, and tzatziki, along with warm pita and vegetable crudités, organized aisle-by-aisle with exact quantities.

3. Adapt menus for dietary restrictions without sacrificing flavor.

Accommodating dietary restrictions makes sure everyone is both safe and well-fed. Edy asks Gemini for quick, creative swaps that meet dietary needs without compromising classic Lebanese flavors. “Modifying the recipes on top of scaling would be incredibly challenging,” says Edy. “So, I have Gemini do all the math and logistics for me." Gemini delivers instant adjustments that keep every menu item authentic, flavorful, and in line with guests’ dietary needs.

Try this to adapt menus: Adapt a dessert spread of pistachio baklava and salted tahini brownies for guests who are strictly gluten-free and nut-free. Suggest ingredient swaps that preserve the flaky texture and nutty, rich flavor.

For small business owners, Gemini can be a game-changer. “Gemini has freed my time up,” says Edy. “I’m able to spend less time doing administrative tasks and more time introducing people to Lebanese food, our culture, and all of its beautiful flavors.”

entries.title: Introducing Vertical Video Unification with Display & Video 360.
entries.summary: Unify vertical video buys with Google Display & Video 360. See how Unilever boosted reach by 24% using Gemini-powered measurement. Get the details.
entries.content:
Audiences today discover brands and purchase products across a wide range of formats, including vertical video. As customer journeys span so many touchpoints, advertisers need a smart platform that unifies media buying and ads that deliver the best ROI.

We’re introducing Vertical Video Unification with Google Display & Video 360, making it possible to buy and measure vertical video programmatically across channels in one platform. This new solution centralizes vertical video buys from publishers across vertical video into a single workstream.

And with Gemini powering buying, execution, and full-funnel measurement, Display & Video 360 delivers competitive campaign performance without overexposing users to the same ads — benefits that siloed buying strategies can’t replicate.

During initial testing, Unilever’s Hellmann’s and WPP Media achieved a 24% increase in unique reach while reducing cost per unique user by 25%.

entries.title: 5 ways to upgrade your study habits with Chrome
entries.summary: The video shows a whiteboard that says "Keeping Tabs on Google Chrome."
entries.content:
Whether you’re trying to wrap your head around a tough chemistry concept or keep your research organized, here are five ways Chrome can help you get the most out of the school year.

1. Dive deeper into new subjects.

Gemini in Chrome is already a powerful tool for learning about complex topics, letting you ask questions about the research paper you’re citing, visualize a concept you’re struggling to understand, or find the relevant part of a YouTube lecture. To help you get more out of all of the educational content the web has to offer, we’re expanding these capabilities on desktop to include even more types of media, like podcasts and videos on sites other than YouTube.

Listening to a podcast on ancient Rome, or reviewing a recording of your last philosophy lecture? Gemini in Chrome can identify key takeaways, find specific information, or clarify confusing moments for almost any audio or video file once you’ve played it through.

2. Test your knowledge to make concepts stick.

Reading your notes helps, but testing your knowledge is what makes a lesson stick. To help you get the most out of your study guide, Gemini in Chrome can now generate interactive quizzes using the content from your tab. Whether it’s a Google Doc of your physics notes, a research paper on the Byzantine Empire, or a YouTube video about machine learning, Chrome can highlight core concepts and help you check your understanding. This feature is rolling out in English in the U.S. and India on desktop and will be expanding to additional regions and mobile in the coming months.

3. Stay organized for class.

Managing papers and projects across multiple classes often means opening dozens of tabs, creating digital clutter that can derail your focus. Whether you prefer to display your tabs vertically or horizontally, with tab groups you can bring order to the chaos by organizing them based on your courses or projects.

But even with your tabs nicely organized, jumping back and forth between pages can break your concentration. That’s where split view comes in, letting you keep reference materials on one side of your screen while you’re drafting a paper on the other. Because paired tabs stay linked together, you can step away or switch tasks and jump right back into your side-by-side workspace when you’re ready.

4. Learn on any device.

When you're deep into a research session, you don’t want to lose your progress when you step away from your computer. You can already send a tab from your laptop to your phone (or vice versa), but now Chrome makes switching between devices even easier by saving the exact state of your tab when you send it over. This includes your scroll position and partially filled forms. So if you're halfway through a 50-page paper on behavioral economics, you can send it to your phone and pick up exactly where you left during your commute.

5. Customize your study routine.

Chrome is designed to adapt to your unique learning preferences. If you get distracted by cluttered websites, immersive reading mode strips away the visual noise so you can focus on the text. You can even change the font, letter spacing, and contrast level if you struggle to read dense blocks of text.

And if you want to listen to your study materials while you’re on the go or resting your eyes after a long day, Chrome’s read aloud tool will narrate the page. On Android, read aloud’s AI playback capability can even generate a podcast-like conversation based on the page you're viewing.

The school year might be well underway, but it’s never too late to upgrade your study habits. From keeping your tabs tidy to helping you understand tough topics with Gemini, Chrome is the ultimate study buddy for whatever challenges the academic year throws at you.

entries.title: 5 Google Photos updates to make the most of summer memories.

entries.content:

entries.title: Our new health and safety tools are live in the Google Health app.
entries.summary: Pixel Watch users can explore the new health and safety tools in the Google Health app.
entries.content:
Health Guardian features 1 , our new proactive health and safety tools, are rolling out in the Google Health app, giving Pixel Watch users more ways to prioritize their well-being directly from their wrists. Users can set up blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, and sleep breathing quality metrics in the app beginning this week. The tools will be included free with Pixel Watch 3, 4, and 5 devices, with the first trend reports arriving in early October. 2

Fitbit Air users will be able to see their insulin resistance and blood pressure trends with a Google Health Premium subscription later this year.

Backed by clinical research, the new Health Guardian features work continuously in the background to track subtle physiological shifts over time. The Health Guardian features suite also includes our first-of-its-kind Breathing Emergency Detection for Pixel Watch 4 and 5 users in select European countries. It’s designed to automatically prompt a call to emergency services if a user experiences severe drops in blood oxygen. 3

entries.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar
entries.summary: an image with the phrase "Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar"
entries.content:
Building on the momentum of last week's Gemini 3.8 Live launch, today we are excited to introduce Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar — bringing near real-time visual presence to our native live dialogue models. By pairing near real-time video generation with speech, the Live Avatar feature creates an experience that listens, sees, and speaks with a dynamic visual persona.

With precise lip-syncing, natural expressions, and fluid turn-taking, Live Avatar enables enterprises to expand their virtual offerings more interactively. Whether providing engaging customer service or delivering interactive walkthroughs, it transforms digital exchanges into richer, more accessible experiences.

Starting today, Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar is available in Gemini Enterprise.

See how Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar supports a wide range of characters, each with a distinct look, voice, and expressive presence.

More natural and multimodal conversations

Conversation is inherently multimodal: we listen, look, speak, and use facial expressions to communicate. Live Avatar brings these capabilities to enterprise agents. By processing visual and audio inputs simultaneously, it generates enriching conversations for a more comprehensive experience.

Watch how Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar takes in what it sees and hears in near real time, responding with expressive audio and video for a more natural conversation.

Asynchronous tool execution with continuous presence

Beyond visual presence, the feature is backed by Gemini’s advanced reasoning. With asynchronous tool calling, Live Avatar can trigger tool calls and fetch data in the background while continuing active dialogue, handling complex tasks while ensuring an uninterrupted conversational flow.

See how Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar handles complex tasks like checking in a guest at a hotel. Calling tools in the background while the dialogue continues uninterrupted.

Conversational experiences built for global scale

Conversational presence should feel natural and not be limited by languages. Live Avatar features native multilingual speech-to-speech synchronization. The feature dynamically adapts its lip-sync and expressions and can seamlessly transition across 97 languages without degrading video fidelity or introducing visual drift.

Watch how Gemini 3.8 Live Avatar switches between languages mid-conversation, with lip-sync and expressions adapting seamlessly across 97 languages.

A Live Avatar to fit your brand needs

Organizations often need distinct visual identities to fit their brand. In addition to a library of diverse, preset avatars, organizations can customize their Live Avatars. From a high-quality reference image, developers can generate a fully animated, responsive avatar while preserving reference likeness, brand styling, or character identity. Custom avatar creation is currently available only through enterprise allowlisting.

Trust and transparency at its core

We built Live Avatar with strict safeguards designed to respect identity, and keep AI-generated content transparent. All output generated by our AI products is watermarked with SynthID. This imperceptible watermark is woven directly into the audio and video output, helping to ensure AI-generated content remains detectable to help minimise misinformation and misattribution. To explore our comprehensive approach to safety and responsible deployment, read our model card.

Get started with Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar

Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar is available in Gemini Enterprise. Explore the API documentation to get started.
